conviction_note: The findings offset almost exactly (impact_sum 0.0): the political-ad proxies and FOX One retention are positive, the FOX News ratings decline and soft linear peer ads are negative, and the bar is disputed, so every finding is capped small. The scaled number leans slightly up (p_up 55 on abs 6.5) because this name has risen after 5 of its last 7 prints, the option skew pays for calls (-9.9 vol pts), and a -5.4% five-day pullback has taken some of the run-up out of the bar. The two measurements differ in sign only by base rate and positioning, not by evidence.
bar: Disputed, so every size is capped. Revenue: $4.23B (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-10-26, https://finviz.com/news/407862/fox-faces-a-higher-bar-as-world-cup-tail-midterm-ads-and-tubi-collide) vs $4.3B on 15 estimates (https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/fox). Adj. EPS: $1.99 consensus with a $2.14 whisper (Earnings Whispers), vs $2.12 on 3 estimates (therighttrader, fetched 2026-10-30) and $2.04 in an earlier snippet from the same aggregator. Year-ago FQ1 FY26: revenue ~$3.74B, adj. EPS $1.51. No formal company quarterly guide; the qualitative guide is the 2026-08-06 call: World Cup tail in FQ1 weighted to the TV segment, midterm political boosting local stations and Tubi, 'Fiscal 2027 off to an excellent start' (https://media.investor.foxcorporation.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/06205327/FOX-FY2026-Q4-Earnings-Call-Transcript.pdf). FOX has beaten consensus in 8 of the last 8 quarters (therighttrader).
positioning_check: FOXA short interest 48.18M shares, 9.5 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up ~6.7% from 45.2M (9.8 days) at 09-15 (https://massive.com/quote/foxa, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/foxa/short-interest/). Chartmill puts it at 24.5% of float (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/FOXA/ownership/short-interest). This is high, but most of it is very likely merger-arb hedging, not a directional bet: Roku holders receive 0.9693 FOXA shares per Roku share (~$96 cash + stock, https://www.shacknews.com/article/149661/fox-roku-deal-22-billion), and arbitrageurs long ROKU short FOXA against it. It is not a squeeze-prone crowded short, though covering would follow if the deal broke. Options: 25-delta skew -9.92 vol pts (calls bid over puts), put/call OI 0.21, event-implied move 6.18%, ATM IV 45.7%. The market's stated lean is upside. Tape: -5.39% over 5 days, +1.17% over 20 days, 17% below the 52-week high. Earnings Whispers on 10-26 had the stock +11% since the last report at $66.60, with sentiment 'firmly bullish'. It is $63.01 now.

findings.finding: Local-TV political is running above plan into the quarter Fox reports (Jul-Sep 2026). On 2026-09-28 Gray Media raised its Q3 political guide to $188-195M from $165-185M (Aug 7), about +10% at the midpoint, while trimming core ad to -1% to flat. AdImpact raised its 2026 cycle projection to a record $11.6B, with broadcast at $5.6B (+$330M, driven by statewide races), and said on 10-14 that spend plus reservations had passed $10B. Fox told the market in August that midterms would boost its local stations and Tubi in FQ1. Consensus revenue of $4.23-4.30B (+13-15% y/y) already embeds some political; the peer raise suggests the station political line can come in above what was modelled in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FQ1 FY26 (2025-10-30), when the ad line beat, the stock rose +7.73%. Q4 FY26 (2026-08-06), with advertising +78% on the World Cup and the guide that political would come, it rose +5.3%. The advertising line has paid on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The Gray raise and the AdImpact revisions are public and sell-side models should carry them, so this is partly priced. What is not visible is any FOXA-specific estimate raise after 09-28: the only consensus numbers found ($4.23B) are no higher than the $4.3B figure. If the market had fully priced an above-plan political quarter, the stock would not have fallen 5.4% in the five days before the print. Fox's stations are big-market (NY, LA, etc.), where political density per dollar is lower than in Gray's swing-state markets, so the transmission is partial.
findings.independence: AdImpact projection raise (https://adimpact.com/blogs/adimpact-reveals-2026-election-cycle-to-reach-record-11.6-billion-in-ad-spending) and the 10-14 milestone (https://political.org/2026/10/16/2026-midterms-could-become-the-most-expensive-election-cycle-ever-adimpact-data-show/), both different sources from Gray. These are proxies for Fox, not Fox's own number.

findings.finding: FOX News Channel's Q3 2026 audience fell sharply year on year in the quarter being reported. Nielsen via TV Insider (2026-10-02): primetime 2.06M viewers (-17%), A25-54 183k (-24.7%); total day 1.32M (-15.8%), demo 120k (-24.5%). MS NOW rose +16% and CNN +12.8% in prime. FNC ad revenue sits in the Cable segment, which already showed EBITDA -3% in Q4 FY26 on World Cup rights amortisation. Lower demo delivery means more audience-deficiency units and less scatter pricing in Jul-Sep.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FNC ratings are not broken out in the release. FOX News Media's record revenue in FY26 (2026-08-06 call: +400 advertisers) was part of the beat bought +5.3%. No prior print found where an FNC ratings decline was the stated cause of a move.
findings.why_not_priced: The ratings are public, and analysts know a slow news quarter follows a heavy one. But the preview coverage found (Earnings Whispers 10-26) lists Tubi, political, the World Cup tail and digital losses as the swing factors and does not mention FNC audience erosion. If it were priced, the preview risk list would name cable news ad softness, and the skew would not be call-bid. Net of the rest of the company: FNC advertising is perhaps a tenth of quarterly revenue, while TV-segment political and World Cup revenue sit far above it. So this trims the beat rather than reversing it.
findings.independence: Adweek TVNewser Q3 2026 ratings (https://www.adweek.com/tvnewser/here-are-the-3rd-quarter-of-2026-cable-news-ratings/) carries the same Nielsen data, so it is the same underlying source. Comcast's linear-network ad weakness (next finding) is a different source pointing the same way for linear generally.

findings.finding: Peer read after Fox last spoke: Comcast's Q3 2026 (reported 2026-10-22) showed NBCU domestic advertising +14.6% headline but only +0.3% excluding $224M of World Cup (Telemundo). The release says growth came from Peacock, 'offset by lower revenue at our networks'. Core national linear ad ex-events was flat-to-down in exactly Fox's quarter, and the AVOD/streaming leg (Peacock for NBCU, Tubi for Fox) carried the growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved FOXA print where a Comcast read-through was the stated driver. In August, FOX's own ad strength was bought (+5.3%) despite 'mixed' peer ad commentary raised on the call.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer print eight days before Fox's, so partly priced. It is filed small because it mostly confirms what the consensus +13-15% revenue growth already attributes to events (World Cup, political) rather than core. If it had moved Fox estimates, the consensus would have come down after 10-22, and no evidence of that was found. This is a secondary write-up of Comcast's 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001166691/000162828026066863/cmcsa-20260930.htm).
findings.independence: Gray's 09-28 core ad guide cut to -1% to flat (https://finviz.com/news/395784/gray-media-raises-3q-2026-political-advertising-guidance-and-lifts-low-end-of-total-revenue-range) points the same way for core ad. It is the same document as finding 1, so it is not double-counted there: finding 1 is sized net of it.

findings.finding: NFL viewership opened weak in September, inside Fox's quarter. League-wide Week 1 averaged 19.5M per game, down about 13% y/y (season opener -12%), before a Week 2 rebound in which FOX's Chiefs-Bears drew 24.3M. FOX won the Week 1 4:25 window at 20.3M. Most NFL inventory is pre-sold upfront, so the revenue risk is makegoods in September only.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved FOXA print where NFL ratings were the stated driver.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small, and only about four September weeks fall in the quarter. If it mattered, previews would list NFL ratings as a risk, and they do not.
findings.independence: Week 2 rebound (https://frontofficesports.com/article/nfl-viewership-bounces-back-in-week-2/) partly offsets it, from the same outlet.

findings.finding: FOX One retention after its World Cup surge is better than at launch. Antenna counts 2.8M gross sign-ups in June 2026, 93% new to the service (2026-07-22). YipitData (2026-08-21) finds 43.1% of the June cohort had a captured cancellation within 60 days, against 52.4% for the Aug-Oct 2025 launch cohort. That points to a larger retained base feeding distribution revenue in Jul-Sep, consistent with management's 'retention surpassed expectations'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q4 FY26, distribution +5% with FOX One 'exceeding expectations' was part of a print bought +5.3%. FOX One is not separately disclosed in revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Panel data is not in consensus models, and Fox does not disclose subscribers. But a 43% 60-day churn still means a large share of the June cohort left before the NFL season, and both figures are floors (silent cancels). The finding is small and could go either way relative to the sell-side's assumed retention.
findings.independence: Antenna June sign-ups (https://www.newscaststudio.com/2026/07/22/fifa-world-cup-drove-2-8m-fox-one-sign-ups-in-june/) is a different panel but measures acquisition, not retention.

findings.finding: The company's own last word on this quarter was unusually firm. On the 2026-08-06 call Murdoch said 'Fiscal 2027 is also off to an excellent start', with continued ad momentum across national, local and digital in FQ1, and 'one of the strongest upfronts in our history, with double-digit growth in volume'. CFO Tomsic said Tubi and FOX One are running ahead and digital investment is moderating, with 'continued bottom-line improvement' in FY27. The upfront volume growth feeds FQ2+ and is what the call commentary on Nov 2 will extend.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FOX gives no formal guide. Its qualitative 'momentum' calls have preceded up moves on 5 of the last 7 prints (baseline), with a median |move| of 5.18%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: it is the reason consensus sits at +13-15% revenue and the whisper above consensus. It is filed because it is the company-level primary statement that the quarter lands inside, and because a company that said 'excellent start' five weeks into the quarter has a track record (8 of 8 beats). Sized small because it is in the wire.
findings.independence: JPMorgan raised its World Cup revenue estimate to ~$800M from >$600M, and Wells raised FY27 EBITDA to $4.12B, in August (https://www.tradingpedia.com/2026/08/14/fox-gains-as-roku-deal-and-ad-upside-lift-analyst-outlook/). That sell-side follow-through is why this is priced.

findings.finding: The bar is elevated by sentiment. Earnings Whispers (10-26) puts the whisper at $2.14 against $1.99 consensus (+7%), notes the stock had run +11% since the last report while the S&P slipped, and calls sentiment 'firmly bullish', saying 'the market has already priced in much of this optimism'. Since then the stock has fallen to $63.01 (-5.4% over five days), which resets part of that bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Feb 2026 (-3.61%) and Aug 2025 (-3.67%), prints fell after run-ups. In both cases the beat was there and the stock still sold.
findings.why_not_priced: A whisper above consensus is itself the market's expectation, so this describes the bar rather than an unpriced fact. Sized small, and against the call-bid skew it is shrunk. The five-day pullback (cause not found) already removed about half of the run-up the preview described.
findings.independence: Baseline tape: run_up_5d -5.39%, run_up_20d +1.17%, 17% below the 52-week high (sealed baseline). The higher consensus EPS of $2.12 at therighttrader (https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/fox) suggests some estimates already sit near the whisper.

findings.finding: Chief Legal and Policy Officer Adam Ciongoli steps down effective 2026-12-01, while the Roku deal is under a DOJ Second Request (issued 2026-09-08). He becomes an 18-month special advisor on legal, policy and regulatory matters at $1.75M a year, with a $12.6M cash-out of equity. Deputy GC Nicholas Trutanich becomes General Counsel. The 8-K gives no reason.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. No print has turned on a legal-officer change.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since 10-19 and carries no earnings content. The advisory role keeps him on the regulatory file, so it says nothing visible about deal odds. Filed at 0 for completeness; the judges may weigh the timing.
findings.independence: DOJ second request 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001754301/000119312526385979/d176496d8k.htm) for context only.

outside_window.finding: Roku reports Q3 2026 after the close on 2026-11-02, with no call and no outlook because of the pending deal. A Roku miss or beat would move FOXA through the 0.9693 exchange ratio and the arb hedge, but only after the window's closing print.
DOJ Second Request on Fox-Roku (2026-09-08). Closing is expected in H1 CY2027, and any challenge or clearance would land well after the window. Deal-break risk is the driver of the arb short in FOXA.

searched_and_found_nothing: Cause of the -5.39% five-day decline into the print: no dated news, downgrade or filing found for 2026-10-26..10-30. Searched Fox news, media sector moves and Roku arb spread.
FOXA-specific analyst estimate revisions or previews dated October 2026 beyond Earnings Whispers: none found (JPM/Wells upgrades are August).
Nielsen Gauge Tubi share for Jul-Sep 2026: Nielsen is publishing September and October together after a methodology change, and July printed no Tubi figure. Nothing usable.
Local-TV peers reporting Q3 2026 before Nov 2 (Nexstar/TEGNA, Gray, Sinclair, Scripps): none have reported. Gray reports 11-06.

Fox EDGAR since 2026-09-15: 8-Ks of 10-06 (proxy supplement and Delaware disclosure suit; Morgan Stanley fees), 10-14 (item 5.07 Roku/Fox Class B special meeting vote) and 10-20 (CLO change). Form 4s of 09-24 and 10-02 not opened, and no open-market insider buying or selling cluster was surfaced. No senior-notes issuance for the Roku cash leg found yet ($11B bridge plus $1B term loan committed).
FOX One subscriber count after the World Cup (Antenna Aug-Sep): no post-World Cup figure published.

rejected_candidates.detail: The regulatory outcome resolves at the DOJ decision in H1 2027, not in the Nov 2 window. The underlying September headline was not located.

rejected_candidates.detail: A $30 FOXA price contradicts the sealed baseline spot of $63.01. It is an old (2022-era) story relabelled by search, not a 2026 event.

baseline_tension: The evidence nets to zero, while the skew (-9.9, calls bid), put/call OI of 0.21 and the 5-of-7-up history lean up. The only lean I emit (p_up 55) comes from that base rate and the 5-day pullback resetting the bar, not from the findings, so it agrees with the skew rather than cutting against it.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced or disputed: EPS $1.99 / $2.04 / $2.12, revenue $4.23B / $4.3B): capped the largest positive, political, from +0.7 to +0.6.

Rule 7 (sign against a strong call-bid skew, -9.9): FOX News ratings shrunk from -0.8 to -0.6 and the whisper/positioning finding from -0.3 to -0.2. Short interest was looked up; it is high (9.5 days) but mostly merger-arb hedging, recorded in positioning_check.
Rule 1 / in the wire (management's 'excellent start' is the bar itself): shrunk from +0.4 to +0.3.
Rule 9 (net of the rest of the company): the FNC ratings finding was already written net of the TV segment's political and World Cup revenue. Size held after the rule 7 cut.
Rule 5 (proxy vs broad series): the Gray political proxy is backed by the broader AdImpact series, which is filed in independence. Left standing, small.
